displayName: Cloud Run 5xx: more than 10 in 5 minutes on any service
threshold: more than 10 responses with a 5xx status from one service inside a 5-minute window
firing: sGTM's 'no available instance' aborts produced 16 5xx responses in the week to 2026-09-04, spread across six hours on four days rather than clustered at one burst; the policy is expected to fire on the next hour that crosses the threshold, and the record captures it when it does

displayName: Cloud Run instance aborts: 'no available instance' on any service
threshold: more than 3 aborted requests from one service inside 5 minutes (the log-based metric from 12.3)
firing: expected to fire on the next sGTM burst above the threshold; sixteen such aborts were logged in the week to 2026-09-04
runbook: 13.5: 'sGTM not responding' (raise min instances or spread the scheduler)

displayName: Cloud Run container failed to start or crash-looped
logFilter: resource.type="cloud_run_revision" AND severity>=ERROR AND (textPayload:"failed to start" OR textPayload:"container exited" OR textPayload:"Container called exit")
threshold: any Cloud Run log line reporting a container that failed to start or exited (crash loops repeat this line); one notification per 30 minutes per policy
firing: cannot be fired safely: producing it means shipping a revision that crashes; the log filter is validated against Cloud Run's documented startup-failure messages instead
runbook: 13.5: roll back to the previous revision (scripts/deploy-cloud-run.sh promote <revision>)

displayName: Pub/Sub backlog on iampatterson-events-push: oldest unacked message older than 5 minutes
threshold: the oldest unacknowledged message on the push subscription is older than 300 s for 5 minutes
firing: cannot be fired safely without stopping event-stream, which would blank the live overlay for visitors; the metric and subscription id were verified live on 2026-09-04

displayName: Pub/Sub backlog on iampatterson-events-push: more than 100 undelivered messages
threshold: more than 100 undelivered messages on the push subscription for 5 minutes
firing: as above: not fired on purpose; the same runbook entry covers it

threshold: any error-severity Cloud Scheduler execution log — a failed attempt on one of the three data-generator jobs; one notification per 30 minutes
firing: fired for real, unrehearsed, on 2026-09-04 at 20:40 UTC — hours after it was created. Cloud Run aborted the `data-gen-leadgen` request for want of an instance and returned 500; the scheduler logged AttemptFinished with status INTERNAL (`URL_UNREACHABLE-UNREACHABLE_5xx`), the policy matched, and the notification arrived at ops-email. This is the first conditionMatchedLog policy in the project to notify, so the log-match kind is proven end to end, delivery included. Record: docs/verification/2026-09-04-first-real-alert.md

threshold: any error-severity log from a Dataform repository — a workflow invocation that completed FAILED; one notification per 30 minutes
firing: cannot be fired safely, and the window in which it could be has closed: the filter was validated against 28 real FAILED completions in the 30 days to 2026-09-04 (`iampatterson_assertions.assert_volume_anomaly`, 'expected zero rows'), but Phase 12 corrects that assertion, and producing a Dataform error on demand otherwise means breaking a scheduled transform. `apply.sh rehearse-dataform` refuses before spending a production workflow run and records the refusal. The condition and filter are proven against the 28 real entries, and the conditionMatchedLog notification path is proven by the Cloud Scheduler policy's unrehearsed firing on 2026-09-04; what this policy lacks is a firing of its own, which nothing in the project can now produce on demand

displayName: BigQuery billed scan above 1 TB in a day
threshold: more than 1 TB of billed scan in a day, about $6 at on-demand pricing and an order of magnitude above the demo's normal day
firing: cannot be fired safely: producing it means spending the money it exists to catch; the metric name is Google's documented BigQuery metric

threshold: any budget_threshold event from the proxy (it logs one per instance at 50, 80 and 100 % of the daily cap)
firing: cannot be fired safely without spending toward the cap; the event and its label are counted by the 12.3 metric
runbook: 13.5: 'Claudish proxy over budget' (kill switch, revert, golden gate)

threshold: any capacity_no_budget event (the cap or the kill switch is refusing translations)
firing: fired on purpose by rehearse-policy: the kill switch is turned on, one translation is requested, the event is counted, the switch is turned off; the record names the date

displayName: TLS certificate expiring within 14 days on a monitored surface
threshold: fewer than 14 days until the certificate expires on any of the five uptime-checked hosts
firing: cannot be fired safely: the certificates are managed and renew on their own; the metric is populated by the 12.2 uptime checks and the record shows the current days-to-expiry per host
